title: Building Systems That Hold Up
paragraphs: I'm a Computer Science Major focused on building dependable, practical software across the stack. I don't chase hype or over-engineer solutions, I focus on picking the right tool for the job and making sure it holds up under real usage.

My work spans web applications, AI orchestration pipelines, and low-level reverse engineering tools. I'm drawn to systems thinking: understanding how different pieces integrate, where the single points of failure lie, and what happens when software breaks in production.

I value simplicity, reliability, and reversibility. Whether building zero-dependency web interfaces, wiring multi-model speech pipelines, or analyzing compiled binaries at the systems level, my goal is always the same: software that solves concrete problems without unnecessary complexity.
quote: Complexity is a liability until proven necessary. Every decision should be simple, safe, and reversible.

subsections.title: Web & Systems
subsections.description: Full-stack development with modern frameworks. REST APIs, databases, and authentication. I care about systems staying up, not just going up.

subsections.title: AI & Orchestration
subsections.description: LLM routing, custom Kokoro TTS speech pipelines, and Live2D interactive avatars. Wiring models together into tools people can actually use.

subsections.title: Reverse Engineering
subsections.description: Static and dynamic binary analysis, inspecting memory layouts, and understanding systems from the inside out.

subsections.title: Creative Tech
subsections.description: Live2D Cubism, game development, and digital music production. Code that intersects with art, sound design, and interactive media.

thought: From zero-dependency mathematical UI to AI orchestration and encrypted storage, building software that solves concrete problems.
title: Featured Projects
paragraphs: A collection of software systems, developer utilities, and interactive applications I've engineered. Each project represents an effort to solve real-world friction — whether that means eliminating bloated framework dependencies, orchestrating multi-model AI pipelines, or writing zero-knowledge cryptographic layers.
I focus on writing software that holds up under real usage, respects system memory, and stays maintainable over time.
quote: Working code beats perfect architecture every time. Build the smallest thing that solves the problem, then refine it.

thought: Hands-on projects teach you how to build; solid fundamentals teach you how things work under the hood.
title: Foundations & Certifications
paragraphs: While self-directed projects teach you how to build, formal certifications and coursework ensure the underlying principles are solid. I use structured curricula to validate core knowledge in data management, network security, and web standards.

Understanding how relational databases organize schemas and ensure data integrity, how network protocols guard against vulnerabilities, and how runtimes manage asynchronous events gives practical development a dependable backbone.
quote: Understanding core fundamentals makes every layer of software above them easier to design, build, and debug.

thought: Exploring diverse interests outside the main track keeps curiosity sharp and brings fresh perspective to software engineering.
title: Explorations & Other Interests
paragraphs: Software engineering doesn't happen in a silo. Beyond web systems and formal coursework, I spend time exploring other creative and technical domains that keep me curious and challenge how I think about problems.

From experimenting with digital music and sound design to prototyping interactive mechanics and exploring low-level system behavior, these side pursuits provide space to build, experiment, and learn freely.
Tinkering across different mediums reinforces fundamentals and keeps the craft engaging. Exploring outside high-level abstractions brings a broader perspective back to day-to-day software design.
quote: The best insights often come from outside your primary domain. Creative tinkering teaches you how to learn anything from first principles.

title: The Toolkit
paragraphs: I don't chase hype cycles. I pick tools that hold up in production, and I work by three words: Simple, Safe, Reversible.
quote: I'd rather spend an hour preventing a bug than a day debugging one in production. Complexity is a liability until proven necessary.
